Notes: Uncoloured (PaintType 2) tiling pattern selected through [/Pattern /DeviceCMYK] with the page's own /DefaultCMYK ICC profile. Fixed in #1373.

Target.Reason: ISO 32000-2 §8.7.3.3 decides this page, not a majority: an uncoloured (PaintType 2) tiling pattern's content stream shall not specify colour, so the cell paints in the tint from `1 0 0 0 scn`, resolved through the page's own /DefaultCMYK profile. Transforming 100% cyan through that profile (obj 12, CMYK->Lab, LittleCMS) gives sRGB (0,158,224) -- exactly what Ghostscript renders and within one unit of mutool. pdftocairo renders (109,78,55) because Poppler honours the cell's own `sc`; it is a reference that is wrong here, which is why this page must NOT be pinned to it.

1.QualityReason: excise renders the dominant non-white colour as (0,157,224) at 150 DPI, matching mutool exactly and Ghostscript to one unit, and matching the page's own ICC profile. Remaining differences against the references are edge/antialiasing placement.
1.Notes: Re-reviewed 2026-09-09 against excise, mutool, Ghostscript, pdftocairo, PDFBox and PDFium. This page was previously pinned Mode=ACCEPTED_REFERENCE/Primary=pdftocairo with agreeingOracles:1, which enshrined the defect: excise painted brown (107,77,55) because it honoured the cell's `/DeviceCMYK cs 0.6875 0.765625 0.8671875 0 sc`. The prior contract described that as excise 'preserving Poppler screen-preview colour semantics' while 'MuPDF/Ghostscript choose a visibly different cyan policy' -- there was no policy choice; the spec and the document's own profile both say cyan. #1373 filed this as a /DefaultCMYK substitution failure, which was also wrong: the substitution resolved correctly the whole time.
